title: AI-Enabled Security Benchmarks for FR3 Ultra-Massive MIMO 6G IoT Networks: Network Intrusion Detection and Angle-of-Arrival Spoofing Detection
content: This paper presents two related benchmark studies of AI-enabled security for FR3 (7-24 GHz) ultra-massive MIMO (UM-MIMO) 6G IoT networks, addressing two different layers of the security stack. Study 1 evaluates machine learning approaches for network-layer intrusion detection using a telecom-relevant benchmark dataset (UNSW-NB15), cross-validating multiple classifiers and reporting a systematic literature synthesis, data-quality audit, and hyperparameter-tuned test-set performance comparison. Study 2 evaluates physical-layer angle-of-arrival (AoA) spoofing detection for FR3 UM-MIMO IoT authentication, benchmarking equal and adaptive snapshot-allocation policies for multi-device authentication under a shared sensing budget, validated against closed-form Cramer-Rao bound theory. Together, the two studies show that AI-enabled security benchmarking must be evaluated separately at each layer, network-layer intrusion detection depends primarily on model choice, hyperparameter tuning, and data-quality awareness, while physical-layer spoofing detection depends primarily on how a shared sensing budget is allocated across devices, indicating that a defence-in-depth FR3 UM-MIMO IoT security posture needs distinct, layer-appropriate AI benchmarking rather than a single unified approach.
